Adaptive.description:
Design 13: the detector reacted to ``warmup_reactions`` of the first
``skipped_after`` distinct values of the field, none or at most
``detection.rare_share`` of them, so later values other than probes were
not tested. ``diagnostic`` points to the warning raised when a probe
reacted after a warm-up without any reaction.
Adaptive.title: Adaptive

AnalysesBlock.description:
What the second pass did for this Report (design 20.1, rule R1).

``mode`` says who decided: ``auto`` (the planner, on benefit and cost),
``forced`` (``--deep`` or ``deep.mode`` ``force``) or ``off`` (``deep.mode``
``off``). ``outcome`` is ``ran`` (analyses were computed), ``reused`` (stored
results were enough), ``nothing_selected``, ``disabled``, ``unavailable``
(the analyses that need the source could not read it: ``reason`` says why and
each is ``skipped`` in ``deep``) or ``failed`` (an automatic second pass met
an error and the Report goes without it). ``deep`` is the second-pass
document, the plan with what it kept, left out and why, and the results; it
is absent when no plan was made.
AnalysesBlock.title: AnalysesBlock

AnalysisPlan.description:
What to add to a Scan, why, and at what cost.

``plan_id`` is the SHA-256 of the rest of the plan. ``executable`` is false
while a selected analysis has no implementation in this version.
AnalysisPlan.title: AnalysisPlan

AnalysisResult.description:
One analysis of one field. ``key`` identifies its inputs (design 20.4):
the Scan, the analyzer and its version, the field, the method and its
effective parameters, and the domain of the values. A result is reused
when the key is the same, whatever the budgets. ``reason`` and ``detail``
explain a status that is not ``complete``; a detail never holds a value
of the data.
AnalysisResult.title: AnalysisResult

Applicability.description: Whether the analysis concerns the field; ``reasons`` are codes.
Applicability.title: Applicability

BaseScan.description:
The base a Report stands on (design 19.5): the identity of the Scan it
holds, so that the base can be recognized, compared and extracted.
BaseScan.title: BaseScan

BinnedHistogram.description:
Counts per bin, exact for the declared classification (HIST-05): bin
``i`` is ``[edges[i], edges[i+1])`` and the last one is closed on the right
so that the maximum belongs to it. The distribution inside a bin is
unknown, so the median and quantiles are estimates with their bounds.

``strategy`` is the one in force and ``requested_strategy`` the one asked
for; they differ, with ``reason``, when the sample could not place the
bounds. ``bounds_source`` says where the inner bounds come from: ``range``
(equal widths between the exact minimum and maximum), ``rows`` (quantiles
of the row sample), ``distinct`` (quantiles of the bottom-k sample) or
``grid`` (the multiples of a power of two of the values with a unit beyond
``max_values``, design 20.19).
``edges`` are written as numbers; the classification used the exact bounds,
so an edge that is not representable may be rounded here.
BinnedHistogram.title: BinnedHistogram

Budgets.description:
Deterministic budgets (design 20.2). Memory is charged with the firm
``max`` bound of each state.

``memory_bytes`` is the hard budget: no selection exceeds it, whoever asked
for it (MEM-06). ``automatic_memory_bytes``, ``max_cells`` (cells of the
common reading) and ``automatic_max_cpu`` limit what the planner picks by
itself; a selection beyond them, because it was requested or forced,
requires a confirmation (R1). Values come from the cost model.
Budgets.title: Budgets

ByLength.description:
Samples by length of the original text (design 18.7), a stratum for each
of at most ``max_lengths`` tracked lengths with ``per_length_k`` values each.

A stratum lists the ``id`` of its values; one that is already in the
``listed`` of ``samples`` is not copied, ``listed`` here holds the others and
its ids continue the numbering of the sample. ``limited`` says that some
stored values are in no stratum: ``other`` sums them. ``max_lengths`` is the
number in force, ``requested_max_lengths`` the one asked for when the memory
budget (design 18.10) granted fewer.
ByLength.title: ByLength

Candidate.description:
One analysis of one field with its decision. ``method`` and ``parameters``
are absent for an analysis that does not apply; ``costs`` too. An analysis
of a pair of fields names the second one in ``partner`` (and ``display``
names both) and carries the ``exploration`` that proposed it.
Candidate.title: Candidate

CandidateRule.description:
A relation learned from the data: rows of ``category`` take the class
``column`` with ``confidence`` over ``support`` classified rows, ``exceptions``
excepted. It is a candidate and never a rule of the data: a rule a user
approves is another thing, with its own provenance (REL-15).
CandidateRule.title: CandidateRule

CardinalityComplete.description: Exact distinct count of the original values (design 9.1).
CardinalityComplete.title: CardinalityComplete

CardinalityEstimate.description:
KMV estimate of the distinct original values (design 18.5).

``value`` is held within the certain bounds of the envelope;
``unclamped_value`` is the raw estimator, present only when a bound
changed it. ``theta_hex`` (the sample threshold) is absent for a sensitive
field: it is the priority of one of its values. A field with long texts
has two disjoint domains: ``parts`` gives each (the estimate is their sum)
and ``k`` and ``theta_hex`` are then those of the parts.
CardinalityEstimate.title: CardinalityEstimate

CardinalityLimited.description:
Distinct count that stopped being tracked (design 9.1).

``upper_bound`` is the certain maximum (the analyzed values);
``threshold_reached_at_record`` and ``overflow_detected_at_record`` are the
records where the table reached its limit T and where T + 1 values were
proven, for the reason ``distinct_limit`` only.
CardinalityLimited.title: CardinalityLimited

CategorySummary.description:
A category against the classes. ``rows`` are all its rows, ``classified``
those in the table, and ``coverage`` their share: a category whose values are
mostly missing says little. ``dominant`` is the index of the class that holds
most of it (a tie goes to the first class listed) and ``purity`` its share of
the classified rows; the other rows are its ``exceptions`` (REL-13).
CategorySummary.title: CategorySummary

ColumnAdvice.description: Whether one column is a good stratification key, and why.
ColumnAdvice.title: ColumnAdvice

CombinationAdvice.description: The strata of several columns taken together.
CombinationAdvice.title: CombinationAdvice

CommonCost.description:
The reading shared by every selected analysis: parsed once, whatever the
number of analyses (COST-01).
CommonCost.title: CommonCost

Costs.description:
What one analysis adds to the common reading (COST-01): its states and
its CPU class.
Costs.title: Costs

Coverage.description:
Design 12.2: ``tested = eligible - not_tested`` and ``tested = matched +
ambiguous + invalid + not_matched``. ``share_tested`` is ``null`` when no
value was tested.
Coverage.title: Coverage

CrosstabResult.description:
The table of the rows of each category by class of a feature of another
column, over every row (REL-11 to REL-15). The counts are exact; ``rows`` is
``counted`` (the table) plus the ``excluded`` rows, and the margins add up to
``counted``. Purity and Cramér's V are computed from the counts in float64.
It shows an association between two columns, not a cause. ``source`` says
whether the rows were read from the source or are the complete sample of the
Scan.
CrosstabResult.title: CrosstabResult

CrosstabSettings.description:
How tables of a category against a feature of another column are explored
and computed (design 20.13, REL-01 to REL-03, REL-11 to REL-16).

A table has at most ``max_categories`` category rows (the most frequent
values, the rest is ``other``) and at most ``max_classes`` class columns,
``other`` included for the lengths, the prefixes and the values; a column with more than
``max_distinct`` distinct values is not a category. ``prefix_length`` is the
number of characters of a prefix. ``examples`` exceptions are kept per cell
and ``max_exception_cells`` cells at most are listed as exceptions (the
result says whether that was all of them).
A category whose dominant class takes ``rule_purity`` percent of at least
``rule_support`` classified rows gives a candidate rule. The exploration
reads the row sample, never the source: ``max_columns`` and ``max_work``
(tables times rows coded) bound its cost, ``max_candidates`` tables at most
are written in the plan and ``automatic_tables`` of them at most are chosen
without being asked. ``explore_min_rows`` is the smallest number of rows a
table needs in the sample to be scored.

Everything that changes a result is part of the key of that result; the
budgets of the exploration are not.
CrosstabSettings.title: CrosstabSettings

CurrencySettings.description:
Conventions of the number part of amounts, set independently of
``detectors.number``.
CurrencySettings.title: CurrencySettings

DatasetProfile.description:
One scan dataset: the rows of a CSV, or the records of a JSON document
or collection (design 5).
DatasetProfile.title: DatasetProfile

DatasetStructure.description: Shape of a JSON dataset; null for CSV sources.
DatasetStructure.title: DatasetStructure

DeepResult.description:
The second-pass document. It is ``complete`` when every analysis of the
plan that can run has a complete result, ``partial`` otherwise.
DeepResult.title: DeepResult

DeepRun.description:
What the latest run did. ``source_verified`` says that the digest of the
reading was compared with the Scan's (PASS2-01); a run that read nothing,
because every result was reused, has none. ``cells_read`` counts the cells of
the fields the analyses read, not of the whole source.
DeepRun.title: DeepRun

DeepSettings.description:
What the second pass computes beyond the plan: the number of bins of a
histogram and where their bounds come from, how pairs of numeric columns
and tables of categories are chosen, how values with a unit are extracted,
and how residual and repeated values are kept.

``linear`` splits the exact range of the Scan into bins of equal width;
``sample_quantile`` places the inner bounds at quantiles of the row sample
(the shape of the occurrences) or, without enough rows, of the bottom-k
sample (the distinct values), for a very skewed distribution. The outer
bounds are always the exact minimum and maximum, and the counts per bin
are exact in both.
DeepSettings.title: DeepSettings

DeepTimings.description:
Where the seconds of a run went: reading and parsing the source, then the
analyses; the rest is setup and assembly.
DeepTimings.title: DeepTimings

DenseHistogram.description:
Exact count of every integer of a small domain: the cardinality, the
mode, the median and every quantile follow from it exactly (HIST-07).
``values`` lists the integers that occur, in ascending order.
DenseHistogram.title: DenseHistogram

Derived.description: Analyses computed after the scan from its samples (specification 5.2).
Derived.title: Derived

DerivedPatterns.description:
Structural patterns inferred from the samples, one entry per field
(design 18.12). They are distinct from the configured ``pattern:<id>``
detectors.
DerivedPatterns.title: DerivedPatterns

DetectorFailed.description: A failure is never reported as values that did not match (CA19).
DetectorFailed.title: DetectorFailed

DetectorProfile.description: What one detector recognized in a column (design 12.3).
DetectorProfile.title: DetectorProfile

DigestInfo.description: Function that gives a long text its digest (design 18.6).
DigestInfo.title: DigestInfo

DistinctCount.description:
Exact number of distinct original values of a field (EXACT-07), in the
domain of the Scan's cardinality (design 21): decoded, before any
normalization. ``values`` is V, the content values the cardinality is taken
over (empty, blank, marker and null cells are not values), ``redundant`` is
``values - distinct``: the occurrences beyond the first of each value, not
the number of values that occur more than once. ``unique`` is ``distinct ==
values`` for this domain.
DistinctCount.title: DistinctCount

DistinctLimited.description:
What a stopped exact count proves (D08): the distinct values met in the
``values_read`` values before the memory budget stopped the field. It is a
lower bound, never the cardinality.
DistinctLimited.title: DistinctLimited

DuplicateResult.description:
The repeated values of a field, or of a combination of columns (design
20.21). ``values`` are the values read (for a combination, the rows where
every column has a value, and ``incomplete`` those where one lacks);
``distinct`` is exact, ``redundant`` is ``values - distinct`` and ``unique``
says that nothing repeats. ``records`` says that the first record of each
value is given, which needs the source. A value is identified by a 128-bit
digest when the source is read: two values collide with a probability under
one in 10^20 for a billion values.
DuplicateResult.title: DuplicateResult

DuplicateSettings.description:
How the repeated values of an identifier or of a key are reported
(design 20.21).

``max_listed`` repeated values are listed, the most repeated first;
``max_tracked`` distinct repeated values at most are counted (beyond, the
occurrences of new ones are only counted). ``records`` asks for the first
record of each value even when the Scan already holds every distinct value,
which makes the second pass read the source. All are part of the key of a
result.
DuplicateSettings.title: DuplicateSettings

DuplicateValue.description:
A value, or a combination of values, found more than once: all its
``count`` occurrences (exact: it was tracked from its second sighting, with
the first one counted) and, when the source was read, the record of the
first. A combination is written as its values in the order of ``columns``.
DuplicateValue.title: DuplicateValue

DuplicatesLimited.description:
What a stopped search for repeated values proves (D08): in the
``values_read`` values met before the memory budget stopped it, at least
``distinct`` distinct values and ``repeated`` repeated ones. Never a
count.
DuplicatesLimited.title: DuplicatesLimited

EstimatePart.description:
One of the two disjoint domains of an estimate that adds up: the values
stored in the sample (``values``) and the long texts (``long_texts``),
each exact or estimated by KMV (design 18.6).
EstimatePart.title: EstimatePart

Evidence.description:
First distinct analytical values of each state, bounded by
``limits.max_evidence_examples``.
Evidence.title: Evidence

ExcelSettings.description:
The table read from an Excel workbook: a sheet or a named table, and the
1-based sheet row of the header of a sheet (``null``: detected).
ExcelSettings.title: ExcelSettings

ExcelSourceInfo.description: The table read from a workbook: where it is and what its header says.
ExcelSourceInfo.title: ExcelSourceInfo

ExceptionCell.description:
A cell that is not the dominant class of its category, with the exact
``count`` of its rows and the first of them in source order.
ExceptionCell.title: ExceptionCell

ExceptionExample.description:
A row of an exception: its record and the value of the second column,
cut at 64 characters.
ExceptionExample.title: ExceptionExample

Execution.description:
How the analysis would run. A refusal to select never means the analysis
is impossible (PLAN-06). ``on_limit`` is the policy when a limit is met
while running (D08): the result is ``limited`` with its reason, and the
count of what was read so far is never presented as complete.
Execution.title: Execution

Exploration.description:
What the row sample says of a pair of numeric columns (design 20.12,
REL-05): the rows both columns have a number in (``pairs``), the
coefficient over them and its interval, or the ``reason`` it is not defined.
It is an exploration of ``scope`` rows and says nothing of the population
beyond them: a pair not detected here may still hold elsewhere. The figures
are rounded to six decimals, which keeps the plan the same on any machine.
``score`` is the lower bound of the absolute coefficient that the planner
ranks by. The ``rank_*`` members are the same for the Spearman coefficient
of the sample (design 20.22): a monotone relation that is not a line has a
low ``score`` and a high ``rank_score``, and the pair is rated by the larger
of the two.
Exploration.title: Exploration

ExploredDataset.description:
The exploration of the pairs of one dataset (design 20.12, REL-06).

``rows`` are the rows of the sample the pairs were scored on, ``scope`` which
rows they are. ``numeric`` columns were looked at; those left out are counted
by reason in ``excluded`` (``constant``, ``sensitive_exposure``,
``repeated_path``, ``identifier_like``, ``not_in_sample``, ``too_few_values``,
``column_budget``) and ``columns`` were kept. Of the ``possible`` pairs,
``evaluated`` were scored, ``undefined`` of them have no coefficient (their
reasons counted in ``undefined_reasons``) and ``listed`` are candidates of
the plan. ``work`` is the pairs times the rows compared, the post-processing
budget (COST-05). ``unavailable`` says why the dataset was not explored.
ExploredDataset.title: ExploredDataset

ExploredTables.description:
The exploration of the tables of one dataset (design 20.13, REL-11).

``categories`` columns are eligible categories and ``features`` the tables
of a column against a feature that were possible: of the columns looked at,
those left out are counted by reason in ``excluded_categories`` and
``excluded_features``. Of the ``possible`` tables, ``evaluated`` were scored
on ``rows`` rows of the sample (``scope`` says which), ``undefined`` have no
score (reasons in ``undefined_reasons``) and ``listed`` are candidates of
the plan. ``work`` is the tables times the rows coded, the post-processing
budget (COST-05); ``cells`` the largest table of the plan, rows by classes,
counters included. ``unavailable`` says why the dataset was not explored.
ExploredTables.title: ExploredTables

FieldPatternsFailed.description:
The inference raised on this field: the other fields and analyses are
unaffected and ``diagnostic`` points to the ``pattern_inference_failed``
error (the exception type only: its message could quote a value).
FieldPatternsFailed.title: FieldPatternsFailed

FrequencyTable.description:
Exact count of every distinct analytical value of a field, each with its
native type, from the most to the least frequent (ties by text, then by
type), as the Scan orders its listing. ``modes`` are the values tied for the
most frequent, ten at most.
FrequencyTable.title: FrequencyTable

Interpretations.description:
Detectors whose ``share_eligible`` reaches ``detection.minimum_share``;
``primary`` only when exactly one qualifies (design 12.4).
Interpretations.title: Interpretations

LengthDistribution.description:
Exact count of every length, in characters of the analytical text, of the
content strings of the field: the domain of ``string_lengths`` in the Scan.
LengthDistribution.title: LengthDistribution

LengthOther.description:
What the strata by length do not hold: ``lengths`` distinct lengths that
are not tracked and the ``occurrences`` counted while they were not
(design 18.7). The strata and ``other`` add up to every stored value.
LengthOther.title: LengthOther

LengthStratum.description:
The values of one length, a bottom-k sample of the originals.

``ids`` number entries of ``samples.listed`` or of ``by_length.listed``;
``kept`` of the ``of`` values sampled are listed (exposure withholds them).
``count_accuracy`` is ``exact`` when the length was tracked from its first
occurrence; ``partial`` when it was admitted late, and then the counts cover
the occurrences from ``tracking_started_at_occurrence`` on (LEN-05).
``selection`` is ``all`` while the stratum dropped no value.
LengthStratum.title: LengthStratum

Limit.description:
What the scan could not establish (QUAL-04): a measure stopped by a
limit, a sample that was cut or withheld, a structure that was truncated.
A limit is never a defect of the data. ``measure`` is the location in the
dataset or field; ``diagnostic`` points to the error of a failed analysis.
Limit.title: Limit

LongTextEntry.description:
A sampled long text: bounded preview, original sizes and digest of the
complete content, which is its identity (design 18.6).
LongTextEntry.title: LongTextEntry

LongTexts.description:
Sample of the values longer than ``limits.max_stored_value_length``.

``occurrences`` counts every occurrence of a long value, exactly. ``of``
long texts are sampled, ``kept`` listed (exposure can withhold them). Like
``Samples`` it is ``all`` until a text was dropped, then ``bottom_k``; ``k``
is the size granted (design 18.10), ``requested_k`` the one asked for when
the budget made it smaller.
LongTexts.title: LongTexts

MarkerCount.description:
One marker or unit: ``count`` values are written with it, ``parsed`` of
them have a number (the others are ambiguous), ``share`` is ``count`` over
every value written with a marker.
MarkerCount.title: MarkerCount

MarkerEnumeration.description:
The markers or units as an enumeration of the values written with one
(parsed or ambiguous): exact counts of every marker, ``listed`` by
decreasing count then text (``truncated`` beyond 1,000), the ``modes`` and
the share of the first one.
MarkerEnumeration.title: MarkerEnumeration

MarkerLayout.description:
How the values with a marker are written: the marker ``before`` or
``after`` the number, with a space between them (``spaced``) or not.
MarkerLayout.title: MarkerLayout

MeasureGroup.description: The numbers written with one marker or unit.
MeasureGroup.title: MeasureGroup

MeasureLevel.description:
The numbers of one population of values with a unit or a marker: the
whole field, one marker, or the markers beyond ``max_groups``.

``numeric`` has the members of the ``numeric`` block of the Scan, computed
the same way, with ``coverage`` the share of the content values of the
field. Its median is exact when the numbers were counted in a table, and
``limited`` (``max_values``) when they went on in bins, whose ``histogram``
then holds the estimate. ``distinct`` (numbers that differ) and ``modes``
(ten at most) exist only with the table.
MeasureLevel.title: MeasureLevel

MeasureOther.description:
The numbers of the ``markers`` beyond the groups, together. Mixing units
makes their numbers a count more than a quantity.
MeasureOther.title: MeasureOther

MeasureResult.description:
The numbers of the values with a currency marker, a percent sign or a
unit, extracted as the ``detector`` of the Scan reads them (design 20.19).

``values`` are the content values of the field: ``parsed`` have a number,
``ambiguous`` a number part the configuration cannot read one way (counted
and never placed), ``invalid`` the shape of a value that does not hold, and
``unparsed`` the rest; they add up. ``scan_not_tested`` are the values the
Scan's detector did not test (adaptive detection) and this pass read.

``overall`` gives the metrics of a numeric field for every parsed value,
``groups`` the same for each marker, the most frequent first, and ``other``
for the markers beyond ``max_groups``. ``homogeneous`` is false when the
numbers mix markers: no conversion is made, so their overall metrics add
quantities that differ. ``storage`` is ``table`` when every number was
counted exactly (``accuracy`` ``exact``), ``grid`` when the distinct numbers
passed ``max_values`` and every group went on in bins: counts, sums and
extremes stay exact, the quantiles are estimates with certain bounds
(``exact_counts``).
MeasureResult.title: MeasureResult

MeasureSettings.description:
How the values with a unit, a currency marker or a percent sign are
extracted (design 20.19).

``max_groups`` markers or units at most get metrics of their own, the most
frequent first; the others are summed up in ``other``. ``max_values``
distinct pairs of a marker and a number are counted exactly; beyond, every
group goes on in bins whose width is a power of two, with exact counts and
moments and estimated quantiles. Both are part of the key of a result.
MeasureSettings.title: MeasureSettings

Memory.description:
Bytes of a state in three scenarios. ``max`` is a firm bound taken from
the counts of the Scan, ``min`` what the Scan already proves and
``expected`` the likely size. They are payloads of the structures, not a
promise of process memory.
Memory.title: Memory

NumberSettings.description:
``dot``: decimal point, thousands grouped by ``,`` or a space; ``comma``:
decimal comma, thousands grouped by ``.`` or a space (design 12.10).
NumberSettings.title: NumberSettings

NumericCoverage.description:
The values of the field that the numeric block describes: ``count`` of
the block out of ``of``, the analyzable values (``values.count``).
NumericCoverage.title: NumericCoverage

Objective.description:
What the plan was asked for. ``forced`` is a second pass that was asked
for as a whole (``--deep``): it takes every applicable analysis the hard
memory budget holds, whatever the automatic limits.
Objective.title: Objective

Observation.description:
A finding about the data (QUAL-02), computed from the facts of the scan
by the versioned ``rule`` and never from values.

``status`` says how much to trust it: ``informational`` is a remark that
may be perfectly valid, ``candidate_anomaly`` a signal that a rule cannot
confirm, ``confirmed_issue`` a defect by the structure of the source.
``dataset`` and ``field`` locate it (both absent for the whole scan);
``records`` lists the first record indices, ``patterns`` the inferred
patterns, ``diagnostics`` the diagnostics and ``limited_by`` the limits
that stop its count from being exact.
Observation.title: Observation

ObservationSettings.description:
Observations, quality issues and limits derived from the finished scan
(design 18.13). ``max_items`` bounds the observations and, separately, the
limits that are listed; the summaries count them all.
ObservationSettings.title: ObservationSettings

Observations.description:
Findings of the scan on the data and on itself (design 18.13), derived
from the facts and from ``derived``, without reading the source.

``items`` hold the confirmed issues first, then the candidate anomalies,
then the informational remarks; ``limits`` are apart. At most
``scan.observations.max_items`` of each are listed and ``truncated`` says
that the summaries count more.
Observations.title: Observations

OutsideBins.description:
Values beyond the bounds of the Scan. A source that is the one the Scan
read has none; a count here would make the result ``failed``.
OutsideBins.title: OutsideBins

PatternCandidate.description:
A structural pattern found in the samples of a field (PAT-06).

``examples`` are ids of entries of the field's samples. ``generalization``
is 0 for the structures as read, 1 when adjacent letters were merged and 2
when letters and digits were; ``merged_structures`` counts the structures
the candidate stands for.
PatternCandidate.title: PatternCandidate

PatternConfidence.description:
Heuristic confidence, not a calibrated probability: the share of the
candidate damped by its support, ``share * n / (n + 1)``.
PatternConfidence.title: PatternConfidence

PatternCounts.description:
The inferred patterns of a field counted over every occurrence (PAT-07 to
PAT-09), in the original domain. ``values`` is the content values of the
field (empty cells and null markers are the Scan's ``missing``); they add up:
``matched + other + excluded = values``, with ``matched`` the sum of the
candidates. A value that no candidate reads is an observation of structure,
never an error (PAT-10). ``computed_from`` says whether the source was read
(``source``) or the exact counts of a Scan that holds every distinct value
were enough (``samples``); the result is the same.
PatternCounts.title: PatternCounts

PatternCoverage.description:
Distinct values of the inference population that the candidate takes.
``basis`` is ``all_distinct`` when the population is every distinct stored
value of the field, ``sample`` when it is a sample: a discovery indicator,
never a frequency of the file (specification 10.1).
PatternCoverage.title: PatternCoverage

PatternExcluded.description:
What did not take part in the inference. ``long_text_occurrences`` counts
occurrences of values too long to be stored (their previews never serve:
LONG-05); the others count distinct sampled values.
PatternExcluded.title: PatternExcluded

PatternExclusions.description:
Values the inference leaves out and the validation therefore does not
test: strings longer than ``scan.pattern_inference.max_value_length``, strings
of more than 32 tokens, and values that are not strings (JSON numbers and
booleans).
PatternExclusions.title: PatternExclusions

PatternGrammar.description: The versioned grammar and generalization rules (PAT-04).
PatternGrammar.title: PatternGrammar

PatternInferenceSettings.description:
Inference of structural patterns from the samples (design 18.12).

The inference reads the samples of the finished scan, never the source.
``max_patterns`` bounds the candidates of a field, ``max_value_length`` the
stored values that take part (longer ones are counted as excluded) and
``min_distinct`` the distinct values a candidate needs.
PatternInferenceSettings.title: PatternInferenceSettings

PatternOther.description: The values no candidate takes, with the number of structures they have.
PatternOther.title: PatternOther

PatternOverlap.description: Distinct values that match every pattern of ``patterns`` (PAT-08).
PatternOverlap.title: PatternOverlap

PatternOverlapCount.description:
Occurrences that every pattern of ``patterns`` reads (they are counted
for one of them only, in ``candidates``).
PatternOverlapCount.title: PatternOverlapCount

PatternPopulation.description:
The values the inference read. ``distinct`` took part out of
``available`` usable values (a cap on the population may leave some out).
PatternPopulation.title: PatternPopulation

PatternProfile.description:
A candidate pattern of the Scan, seen over every occurrence: how often it
reads a value, one value it reads (the first one met) with its first record
when the source was read, and the distinct values it reads (``exact``, or
``at_least`` when the sets could not be held).
PatternProfile.title: PatternProfile

PatternTally.description:
Occurrences read by one candidate pattern of the Scan, exclusively: each
value counts for the most specific candidate that reads it (PAT-08).
PatternTally.title: PatternTally

PatternToken.description:
One token of a pattern signature (design 18.12): a class of characters
repeated ``min`` to ``max`` times (characters), or a ``literal`` text
repeated ``min`` to ``max`` times.
PatternToken.title: PatternToken

PearsonExclusions.description:
The rows a pair leaves out, because a value is missing: ``first_missing``
has a number in the second column only, ``second_missing`` in the first only,
``both_missing`` in neither. A value is missing when the row has none, or
it is not a number, or the number does not fit a float64.
PearsonExclusions.title: PearsonExclusions

PearsonResult.description:
Pearson correlation of two numeric columns over every row where both
have a number (REL-07 to REL-09). ``rows`` are the rows examined, ``pairs``
those that count (``pairwise_complete``) and ``excluded`` the others, so that
``rows`` is ``pairs`` plus the three exclusions. The means and spreads are
those of the common rows, not the Scan's. Without ``min_pairs`` common rows,
or when a column does not vary over them, there is no ``coefficient`` and
the ``reason`` says why: never 0. The counts are exact; the coefficient is
computed in float64 (``precision``), from stable co-moments. It measures a
linear association, not a cause (REL-10). ``slope`` and ``intercept`` are
the line of the second column on the first through the same co-moments
(defined with the coefficient), ``r_squared`` the share of the variance of
the second column it explains, and ``rank`` the rank correlation, when asked
for. ``source`` says whether the rows were read from the source or are the
complete sample of the Scan.
PearsonResult.title: PearsonResult

PearsonSettings.description:
How pairs of numeric columns are explored and which are kept (design
20.12, REL-04 to REL-06).

The exploration reads the row sample, never the source. ``max_columns``
and ``max_work`` (pairs times rows compared) bound its cost: the columns
beyond them are left out, and the plan says so. ``max_candidates`` pairs at
most are written in the plan, the best first; ``automatic_pairs`` of them
at most are chosen without being asked. ``explore_min_pairs`` is the
smallest number of rows a pair needs in the sample to be scored and
``min_pairs`` the smallest number a coefficient over every row needs to be
defined. ``rank_bins`` is the number of bins per column of the grid the
Spearman coefficient is read from (0 turns it off, and the exploration stops
rating pairs by rank too); ``min_pairs`` and ``rank_bins`` are part of the
key of a result.
PearsonSettings.title: PearsonSettings

PercentRange.description:
The parsed percentages below 0, from 0 to 100, and above 100: a share
above 100 is a fact of the data, never an error.
PercentRange.title: PercentRange

PercentageSettings.description:
Conventions of the number part of percentages, set independently of
``detectors.number``.
PercentageSettings.title: PercentageSettings

PeriodCount.description:
Values placed in one period: ``period`` is ``YYYY-MM-DD``, ``YYYY-MM`` or
``YYYY`` according to the granularity.
PeriodCount.title: PeriodCount

PeriodCounts.description:
Exact count of the dates of a field per calendar day, month or year
(TIME-01, TIME-02). A value is placed by the calendar date it is written
with: the offset of an aware datetime is not converted, so a change of
daylight saving time moves nothing. ``count`` values are placed, as many as
the Scan counted of this ``temporal_kind``; ``ambiguous`` are the ones whose
day and month order the Scan could not resolve, counted and never placed
(TIME-03); ``unplaced`` is every other content value (not a date, invalid,
or of another kind). ``periods`` lists the non-empty periods in order.
PeriodCounts.title: PeriodCounts

PhoneSettings.description:
``nanp``: Canada, the United States and the other NANP countries;
``fr``: France.
PhoneSettings.title: PhoneSettings

PlanBase.description: The Scan the plan stands on (design 19.5).
PlanBase.title: PlanBase

PostalCodeSettings.description: ``ca``: Canadian postal codes; ``us``: United States ZIP codes.
PostalCodeSettings.title: PostalCodeSettings

PresentationSettings.description:
Report presentation settings: the ``report`` object of configuration
files.
PresentationSettings.title: PresentationSettings

ProvidedRule.description:
A rule a user gave, checked against the table (design 20.22): the rows of
the category named ``category_label`` take the class named ``class_label``.
Unlike a candidate rule it is not learned and needs no support: ``support``
is the classified rows of the category, ``confidence`` the share of them in
the class, ``exceptions`` the others, and ``counter_examples`` the cells
that break it with their first rows. ``status`` is ``holds`` when no row
breaks it, ``violated`` otherwise, ``no_rows`` when the category has no
classified row and ``unknown_category`` or ``unknown_class`` when a label is
not on the axis of the table (``category`` and ``column`` are then absent).
ProvidedRule.title: ProvidedRule

PurityFigure.description: ``dominant`` rows out of ``total``, and their share.
PurityFigure.title: PurityFigure

QualitySummary.description:
What was found, whole scan (``dataset`` absent) or one dataset, counted
before ``scan.observations.max_items`` cuts the lists. ``has_observations``
is any observation, ``has_quality_issues`` a candidate anomaly or a
confirmed issue, ``has_limits`` any limit; they stand for the counts.
QualitySummary.title: QualitySummary

Quantile.description:
A quantile by linear interpolation between the two ranks around it
(``(n - 1) * level``): for the median, the value at the middle rank, or the
mean of the two central values when the count is even. ``exact`` when the
counts are per value; ``estimated`` when read from bins, with ``lower`` and
``upper`` that the value cannot leave.
Quantile.title: Quantile

QuantitySettings.description:
Conventions of the number part of quantities, set independently of
``detectors.number``, and the counted units of ``details``.
QuantitySettings.title: QuantitySettings

RankEstimate.description:
The Spearman rank correlation of a pair, read from a grid of ``bins`` bins
per column cut at quantiles of what the Scan kept (design 20.22): an
estimate, with the ``lower`` and ``upper`` bounds that hold whatever order
the values have inside their bins. ``bins_first`` and ``bins_second`` are
the bins that hold a row; ``edges_first`` and ``edges_second`` say where the
edges of each column come from (``rows``: the row sample, ``distinct``: the
distinct values the Scan kept, ``range``: equal widths, the Scan kept too
little). Without a coefficient the ``reason`` says why: never 0.
RankEstimate.title: RankEstimate

RareMarkers.description:
The markers each written in less than ``share_below`` of the values
with a marker, and the values written with them.
RareMarkers.title: RareMarkers

ReasonCount.description: Occurrences of ``invalid`` values for one reason of the detector.
ReasonCount.title: ReasonCount

Relations.description:
What the planner looked at to propose pairs of columns (``datasets``: one
entry per dataset with at least two numeric columns) and tables of a
category against a feature (``tables``: one per dataset with a category).
Relations.title: Relations

RepeatedValues.description:
The values found more than once: how many (``distinct``) and their
``occurrences`` in all, exactly. Up to ``max_tracked`` of them are tracked
with their count and listed, the most repeated first (``truncated`` when
more are tracked than listed); the occurrences of the others are only
counted in ``untracked``, which makes ``complete`` false.
RepeatedValues.title: RepeatedValues

ReportBlock.description: What a Report adds to the Scan base.
ReportBlock.title: ReportBlock

RequestedAnalysis.description:
An explicit request. ``dataset`` and ``field`` are absent for every
dataset or field; ``candidates`` counts what it matched, 0 when the
analysis does not concern any field asked for.
RequestedAnalysis.title: RequestedAnalysis

ResidualDetector.description:
What a replayed detector made of the strings of the field, beside what the
Scan counted: ``scan_not_tested`` values were not tested by the Scan
(adaptive detection) and were read here.
ResidualDetector.title: ResidualDetector

ResidualResult.description:
The values that patterns and detectors leave out, and the patterns over
every occurrence (design 20.20). ``records`` says that the first record of
each value is given, which needs the source. ``accuracy`` is ``exact`` when
every table is ``complete`` and every pattern distinct count ``exact``, and
``exact_counts`` when occurrences are exact but a list is bounded.
ResidualResult.title: ResidualResult

ResidualSettings.description:
What the values that a pattern or a detector leaves out are kept as
(design 20.20).

``max_listed`` values are listed per source and state, the most frequent
first; ``max_tracked`` distinct values at most are counted per source and
state (beyond, the occurrences of new values are only counted); a value of
more than ``max_value_length`` characters is counted and never listed;
``max_detectors`` detectors at most are replayed per field. ``records``
asks for the first record of each value even when the Scan already holds
every distinct value, which makes the second pass read the source. All are
part of the key of a result.
ResidualSettings.title: ResidualSettings

ResidualTable.description:
What one source leaves out in one state (design 20.20): the values no
candidate pattern reads (``other``), or the values of a detector that are
``invalid`` or ``not_matched``.

``occurrences`` is exact. ``listed`` holds the most frequent tracked values;
``distinct`` counts the tracked ones and is the distinct count when
``complete``. Values beyond ``max_tracked`` are only counted in
``untracked`` (occurrences), and a value longer than ``max_value_length`` in
``too_long``; both make ``complete`` false. ``truncated`` says that more
tracked values exist than are listed. ``reasons`` split the occurrences of
an ``invalid`` state.
ResidualTable.title: ResidualTable

ResidualValue.description:
A value a pattern or a detector leaves out, with the occurrences counted
since its first appearance (so exact) and, when the source was read, the
record of the first one.
ResidualValue.title: ResidualValue

RowPopulation.description:
The records read (``records``) and the ones the middle is drawn from:
positions ``edge`` + 1 to ``records`` - ``edge``, ``interior`` of them
(``scope`` names it, ROW-07).
RowPopulation.title: RowPopulation

RowSample.description:
Common row sample of a dataset: first rows, a bottom-k of the interior
and last rows, the same cells for every projected field (design 18.11).

``middle_k`` is the size of the middle in force, below ``requested.middle``
when the byte budget cut it (``reason`` is then ``memory_budget``, which
also covers start or end rows left out). ``complete`` says that every record
read is a row. ``threshold`` (16 hexadecimal digits) is the largest priority
kept in the middle, written once a middle row was dropped. ``fields`` are
the projected field ids; ``fields_limited`` says that untracked paths are not
projected. ``bytes`` is the modelled size of the rows kept, ``max_bytes`` the
budget of the scan. ``kept`` rows are listed out of the ``of`` sampled: a
Report keeps the header and no row (``kept`` 0).
RowSample.title: RowSample

RowSizes.description:
Sizes asked for: ``rows`` in all, ``edge`` first and ``edge`` last rows,
and ``middle`` = ``rows`` - 2 * ``edge`` rows of the interior.
RowSizes.title: RowSizes

RunCounters.description: Optional diagnostic counters of a run (``scan(counters=True)``).
RunCounters.title: RunCounters

RunInfo.description:
What varies from one run to the next on the same source: it is not part
of the description of the data.
RunInfo.title: RunInfo

SampleEntry.description:
A sampled original value with its exact count (design 18.9).

``id`` numbers the entry in the listing of the Scan and stays the same in a
Report that keeps a subset of it.
SampleEntry.title: SampleEntry

SampleHash.description: Priority function of a bottom-k sample (design 18.3).
SampleHash.title: SampleHash

SampleRow.description:
A row of the row sample: its position in the dataset (the record index),
the groups it belongs to and the cells of the projected fields.

``values`` holds the canonical text per field id, through its exposure: a
list when the path repeats, ``null`` for a JSON null or a hidden cell, no
key for a field absent from the record. ``truncated`` lists the
fields whose cell was cut at ``cell_chars`` (design 18.11).
SampleRow.title: SampleRow

Samples.description:
Distinct original values with their exact counts (design 18.9).

``all`` lists every distinct value, in first-seen order; ``bottom_k`` the
ones of smallest priority, in ascending priority, and names ``k``, the
``hash`` and the ``threshold`` (the largest priority kept, as hexadecimal
digits; absent while no value was dropped and for a sensitive field).

``kept`` values are listed out of the ``of`` the scan sampled: a Scan has
``kept == of`` unless exposure withheld values (``mask`` merges, ``hide``
lists none); a Report keeps fewer (design 19.4) and says so here.
Samples.title: Samples

SamplingCounters.description:
Work of the bottom-k samplers over all fields (design 18.4). Counters
that the scan could not measure are not written; a count of 0 is a
measured zero.
SamplingCounters.title: SamplingCounters

ScanConfig.description: Validated scan settings; every section has defaults.
ScanConfig.title: ScanConfig

Selection.title: Selection

SourceShape.description: Global size of the source, whatever the dataset.
SourceShape.title: SourceShape

State.description:
A piece of memory an analysis needs. Two candidates with the same ``key``
share it, and the plan counts it once (PLAN-04).
State.title: State

Stratification.description: Advice for ``stratified`` sampling and for the choice of its columns.
Stratification.title: Stratification

StratificationLimits.description: The deterministic thresholds the advice was made with.
StratificationLimits.title: StratificationLimits

StructureField.description: One path of a JSON dataset, containers included (design 16.2).
StructureField.title: StructureField

Summary.description: Counts of the candidates by decision, and what the selection needs.
Summary.title: Summary

TableAssociation.description:
Cramér's V of the table over the rows and columns that have a count (the
``effective`` ones; the others stay in the table), or the ``reason`` there is
none: never 0 for lack of data (REL-14). ``corrected`` is the bias-corrected
V. A score is ``stable`` unless the expected counts are low (``low_share`` of
the cells under 5, or one under 1) on the axes that hold at least 5 rows; the
``sparse`` axes, with fewer, only count here. An unstable score is never to be
read as strong.
TableAssociation.title: TableAssociation

TableAxis.description:
One axis of a table: the field it reads, the ``domain`` of the values it
reads (design 21) and its classes in the order of the counts.
TableAxis.title: TableAxis

TableClass.description:
A row or a column of a table: a category value or a class of a feature.
``label`` is what a reader sees (the value, a pattern rendering, a length, a
prefix), ``other`` the class of everything the named ones do not take, and
``type`` the native type of a category of a JSON file that is not a string.
TableClass.title: TableClass

TableExceptions.description:
The rows outside the dominant class of their category (REL-15): ``count``
of them in ``cells`` cells, the ``listed`` largest with their examples.
``complete`` says that every cell is listed; otherwise the list stops at the
bound of the settings (``max_exception_cells``) and ``cells`` tells how many
there are.
TableExceptions.title: TableExceptions

TableExclusions.description:
The rows left out of the table. ``category_missing`` has no category,
``feature_missing`` no value in the second column, ``both_missing`` neither,
and ``unclassified`` a value the feature does not classify (not a string,
longer than the patterns read).
TableExclusions.title: TableExclusions

TableExploration.description:
What the row sample says of a table of a category against a feature of
another column (design 20.13, REL-05): the ``rows`` classified in both
axes, the effective ``categories`` and ``classes`` (axes with a count), and
the association, or the ``reason`` it is not defined. It says nothing of
the population beyond the ``scope`` rows: a relation not detected here may
still hold elsewhere. ``score`` is the bias-corrected Cramér's V the planner
ranks by, and ``stable`` says whether the sample has the counts to trust it (a
table that is not is still listed: the whole file may have them). Figures are
rounded to six decimals.
TableExploration.title: TableExploration

TableFeature.description:
The feature of the second column that makes the classes (REL-01):
``prefix_length`` is the number of characters of a prefix.
TableFeature.title: TableFeature

TablePurity.description:
The purity of the table in the direction category to class (``forward``)
and class to category (``reverse``), which is another figure (REL-13), and
the ``baseline``: the share of the most frequent class, which a rule that
always answered it would reach.
TablePurity.title: TablePurity

TechnicalType.description:
Port of the current type inference (design 9.7): ``confidence`` is the
accepted share, ``null`` without values; ``outside_count`` is ``null`` for
``mixed``.
TechnicalType.title: TechnicalType

TemporalKind.description:
Values of one kind; ``min`` and ``max`` are ISO strings. Aware values
compare as instants; naive and aware values are never compared.
TemporalKind.title: TemporalKind

TemporalStats.description:
Temporal values of the date detector; ``ambiguous`` values are counted
and excluded (design 9.6).
TemporalStats.title: TemporalStats

Timings.description: Where ``RunInfo.duration_seconds`` went; the five parts add up to it.
Timings.title: Timings

Utility.description:
A versioned heuristic from 0 to 100 with its reasons. It orders the
candidates; it is not a measure of the data.
Utility.title: Utility

ValueCount.description: An analytical value in its canonical text, with its native type.
ValueCount.title: ValueCount

ValueExamplesSettings.description:
How the report represents the values of a column. The candidates of its
examples are the ``kept_per_column`` smallest priorities of the scan sample
(``scan.limits.max_samples``), or a draw seeded by ``scan.random_seed`` when
the sample has no priorities.
ValueExamplesSettings.title: ValueExamplesSettings

tabalyst__config__RowSampleSettings.description:
Rows of the scan's row sample that the report keeps and shows: the first
``start`` rows, the ``middle`` rows of the interior with the smallest
priorities (an exact subset of the scan's) and the last ``end`` rows. At
most what the scan kept; presentation, so it never changes the scan.
tabalyst__config__RowSampleSettings.title: RowSampleSettings

tabalyst__models__NormalizationStage.description: One stage of the scan's normalization (design 10), ``raw`` first.
tabalyst__models__NormalizationStage.title: NormalizationStage

tabalyst__models__VariantGroup.description: Raw spellings sharing one comparison key.
tabalyst__models__VariantGroup.title: VariantGroup

tabalyst__scanner__config__RowSampleSett.description:
Row sample of a dataset (design 18.11): ``edge`` first rows, ``edge`` last
rows and a bottom-k of the interior, ``rows`` in all; 0 rows turns it off.

``max_bytes`` is the budget, in bytes of a cost model, of the cells kept by
the whole scan.
tabalyst__scanner__config__RowSampleSett.title: RowSampleSettings

tabalyst__scanner__models__Normalization.description:
``changed`` and ``cardinality`` are ``null`` for a disabled stage and
``changed`` for ``raw``.

``equals`` names the stage whose output this one received (the previous
enabled stage, or ``raw``) when ``changed`` is 0: no occurrence was
modified, so the distinct values are the same and so is ``cardinality``,
complete or limited (design 10). A limited stage that changed something
has no ``equals``: its count is not derived from the raw table (D13).
``cardinality`` of a limited stage never carries the estimate or the upper
bound of ``values.cardinality``, which is where to read them.
tabalyst__scanner__models__Normalization.title: NormalizationStage

tabalyst__scanner__models__Variant.description: A raw string variant of a comparison key.
tabalyst__scanner__models__Variant.title: Variant

tabalyst__scanner__models__VariantGroup.description:
A comparison key with at least two distinct raw variants; ``count`` and
``distinct`` cover every variant, ``variants`` the most frequent ones.
tabalyst__scanner__models__VariantGroup.title: VariantGroup

title: Tabalyst Report
